data.one_liner: Laravel Echo implementation for Flutter supporting Socket.io and Pusher
data.what_it_does: Provides Laravel Echo broadcasting capabilities in Flutter. Supports public, private, encrypted private, and presence channels using Socket.io or Pusher connectors.
use_when: Your Flutter app needs to connect to a Laravel backend broadcasting system
You want to listen to WebSockets via Socket.io or Pusher in Flutter
avoid_when: You do not use a Laravel backend or broadcasting server
You only need standard REST or GraphQL API calls without broadcasting channels
strengths: Supports multiple channel types including public, private, and presence channels
Supports both Socket.io and Pusher connectors
weaknesses: Requires specific companion npm packages and configuration on the server side
data.setup_notes: Requires adding pubspec dependencies for socket_io_client and pusher_client_socket, and optionally installing the fixed-laravel-echo-server via npm on the server side.
